chapter: Postwar: Chicago, Vinson, Hines and Cootie
title: Leaving Vinson in St. Louis; Sil Austin's brother replaces him
summary: He gave notice in San Francisco and left in St. Louis; a new drummer, Sil Austin's brother, lacked the swing.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: No, I didn't leave the package. No, not at all. That was after we came back into New York.
I see.
And went out again, and I left him in St. Louis. But he didn't have a package.
Yeah, I see.
We were playing a dance hall there in St. Louis.
And what did you do?
I put my notice in and told him to get him somebody else.
Yeah.
I put it in in San Francisco and left him in St. Louis.
Yes.
Sil Austin, he's the alto player. Well, his brother was playing drums. His brother played drums with Jonah Jones.
Oh, Austin? The only Austin I can think of is Cuba.
Cuba, the drummer?
Yeah. Cuba used to play with McKinney's. That's not the one, because he'd be older.
Well, he's no baby.
Really?
And Sil Austin played alto, and his brother played drums. When Jonah Jones had all those hits out, on the records.
Yeah, yeah.
Well, he was the drummer of the band.
Yeah, yeah.
If I can think of his name.
Well, never mind. I can tell because Jonah was talking about it the other day.
Well, that's who took my place with Eddie Vinson.
With Eddie Vinson, yeah.
Yeah.
Yeah.
But he didn't make it. He didn't have the right swing for Eddie's band, see.
No, no. And besides, if he was right for Jonah's small group, that wasn't the same thing, was it?
No, it wasn't the same thing at all, see. But Eddie hired him and he met him in St. Louis, and I let him sit in, play that date.
Yeah, yeah.
I wanted to hear how he sounded with the band. Well, he didn't sound -- he didn't have that swing at all. No, not at all.
No, that's very bad. It's so rough on everyone in the band.
But he played all right with Jonah Jones' band, but not with Eddie. Eddie Vinson.
